items.title: Smulyan interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2010
items.q: So when I did my record with strings... Bob Belden, he arranged the music and conducted, and it was really, I mean he held it together and he made that session happen.

ctx.x: I mean think of all the great, thousands of great records that have been done in those kind of situations, two four-hour sessions.

Exactly. And people standing around one mic and just playing. Well I don’t know. It seems like an excessive amount of time to put a jazz record together. For me, it’s like I said, to kind of put something together in six hours and to try to get a moment or capture a moment in time with warts on it — it’s not going to be perfect — I mean there’s no perfect jazz record, no perfect jazz solo. I mean there are some more perfect than others of course. But when I did my record with strings, we did that record in four…
This passion you have for music, is there is precedent for it in your parents or your grandparents or anything? Where’d it come from?
